services.name: Story
services.text: We research your world, find the idea, write it and plan where the film will live.
services.more: Every good film starts with knowing who it's for and what it has to do, and we find that out by asking good questions and checking our sources. Our SITREP research into your craft, your peers and your industry points us to the story worth telling, and then we write it and plan where it will play.
services.includes: SITREP research, concepts, treatments, scripts, storyboards, distribution plans

services.name: Production
services.text: We plan the shoot and run it: casting, locations, directing, camera, light and sound, on the ground and in the air.
services.more: This is everything from the first call sheet to the last shot. We find the right people and places, then bring cinema cameras, lighting, sound and aerials, run by a crew with a decade in the field.
services.includes: Producing, casting, locations, permits, schedules, directing, cinematography, lighting, sound, drone, cable cam, high-speed rigs

services.name: Editing
services.text: We cut, color and finish the film, then make a version for every screen.
services.more: This is where the story comes together. We edit, color, mix and add graphics, then cut a version for every place the film needs to play.
services.includes: Editing, color grading, mixing, motion graphics, subtitles, social cuts

services.name: Photography
services.text: We shoot stills with the same eye: brand imagery, portraits, products and behind the scenes.
services.more: Our stills come from the same eye as our films. We can shoot them alongside the video or on their own.
services.includes: Brand imagery, portraits, products, behind the scenes

services.name: Rentals
services.text: You can rent our cinema cameras, lenses and lighting, with or without our crew.
services.more: Our own cinema kit is available to rent, on its own or with our crew to run it.
services.includes: Cinema cameras, lenses, lighting, crew optional

audiences.name: Nonprofits & public service
audiences.text: We make films for nonprofits, NGOs, tribal councils and public agencies that move people to give, join and act.
audiences.title: Films that move people to act.
audiences.headline: Nonprofit and public service video

faq.q: Can a nonprofit afford you?
faq.a: Projects start around $1,000, and we scope to the budget you have. Tell us the goal and the number, and we'll tell you straight what it buys.

faq.q: Do you work with public agencies and tribal councils?
faq.a: Yes. For the Inter Tribal Council of Arizona we've made WIC nutrition films, vaccine education for its Tribal Epidemiology Center and Your Voice, Your Power, a 10-part docuseries on tribal voting.

work.title: Your Voice, Your Power: Full Episode

audiences.about: The people on camera trust you with their stories, so we treat them with the same care you would. Here's Kelly's Story, which we made with UMOM New Day Centers:
audiences.heading: Dignity comes first.
audiences.intro: A film for a nonprofit or a public agency has one job: to get someone to care enough to act. That might be a donor at a gala, a family deciding whether to enroll, or a lawmaker hearing why water rights matter to a community. We've told these stories for UMOM New Day Centers, New Pathways For Youth, Paradise Valley Mountain Preserve Trust and the Inter Tribal Council of Arizona.
audiences.approach: People share their stories on their own terms, so we plan interviews around their comfort, not our shot list. Budgets have to stretch, too. One shoot should feed the gala, the donor email, the grant report, the briefing with lawmakers and a month of social posts, so we plan those cuts before we roll. And because a moving story isn't enough on its own, every film ends with a clear next step: give, volunteer, sign up, vote or show up. Here are a few of the stories we've told:
points: We work with nonprofits, NGOs, foundations, tribal councils and public agencies.
We do the research first, then put the story first and protect the people on camera.
We make fundraising films, impact stories, PSAs, public education films and docuseries.
The films play at galas, in donor emails and grant reports, in front of lawmakers and across social.

audiences.name: Schools & institutions
audiences.text: We make films for universities, schools, museums, art spaces and research centers that help people learn, visit and believe in the work.
audiences.title: Big ideas, made clear.
audiences.headline: Video for schools and institutions

faq.q: What do schools and institutions use video for?
faq.a: Mostly to explain the work, recruit students and staff, bring in donors and grants, and invite people to visit. One shoot can cover all of them if we plan the cuts up front.

faq.q: Can you explain complex research on camera?
faq.a: Yes. We read up first, then let the people who do the work explain it in their own words, and we add visuals where words aren't enough. We've done it for Nektar's cancer research and for the Inter Tribal Council of Arizona's vaccine education.

audiences.about: Institutions have big ideas and short attention spans to win over, so we look for the person who makes the idea click. Here's Immerse Yourself, which we made for Wonderspaces:
audiences.heading: Teach it, then show it.
audiences.intro: Universities, schools, museums, art spaces and research centers all have the same problem: important work that is hard to explain in a minute. We help them show it instead. We've filmed immersive art at Wonderspaces, vaccine education with the Inter Tribal Council of Arizona's Tribal Epidemiology Center and patient stories for Nektar's research.
audiences.approach: We do our homework before we film, so we can ask the questions that get experts talking like people. We keep it honest and plain, and we let the work speak for itself. Most institutions need more than one film from a shoot, so we plan the recruiting cut, the donor cut and the social cuts before we roll. Here are a few films that fit the bill:
points: We work with universities, schools, museums, art spaces, libraries, foundations and research centers.
We research the subject first, then let teachers, researchers and artists explain it in their own words.
We make explainers, recruiting films, donor and grant films, exhibition films and short documentaries.
The films play in classrooms and lobbies, at galas, in grant reports and on websites and social.

audiences.name: Businesses
audiences.text: We make explainers, culture films and stories that connect people with what a business does, from the bakery down the street to a national company.
audiences.title: The story behind what you do.
audiences.headline: Business video

faq.q: What do businesses use video for?
faq.a: Mostly explainers, educational films, culture and recruiting films, training, and stories that show customers what you do and the people behind it.

faq.q: Can you film at our shop, office or job site?
faq.a: Yes. We come to you, anywhere in Arizona or beyond, and we work around the workday.

audiences.about: Every business has people and a craft worth showing, whether it's one shop or a hundred. Here's Premium Products, Excellent Service, which we made for Citgo and Brundage Bone:
audiences.heading: Your people are the story.
audiences.intro: We work with businesses of every size, from a neighborhood bakery to a chain of doctor's offices to a national company. We make explainers, educational films, culture, recruiting and training films, and stories that help people in your community understand what you do and why it matters.
audiences.approach: We start with research, because a good film needs a point of view, and the best one is usually the thing only you can say. We schedule around your workday and keep interviews quick and painless. One shoot can give you the main film, shorter cuts and stills, plus a library of footage for onboarding, training and your website long after we leave. Here are a few of the films we've made for businesses:
points: We work with businesses of every size, from the shop down the street to national companies.
We take it from research and the first idea to delivery, and we work around your workday.
We make explainers, educational films, culture, recruiting and training films, and customer stories.
The films live on your website and social, in onboarding and training, and with your team in every conversation they have with customers.

You can bring in a full production crew for one shoot or a whole season of work, and when the story is a sensitive one, we treat the people on camera with real care. industries.name: Tribal Nations
industries.text: We make public health, education and civic films with tribal communities, told in their own voices.
industries.title: In their own voices.
industries.intro: We make public health, education and civic films with the Inter Tribal Council of Arizona, which represents 21 tribal nations. The lesson has been the same every time: do the research first, then let community members tell their own stories.

faq.q: Have you worked with tribal governments before?
faq.a: Yes. Our work for the Inter Tribal Council of Arizona includes WIC nutrition PSAs, vaccine education for its Tribal Epidemiology Center and Your Voice, Your Power, a 10-part docuseries on tribal voting.

faq.q: What does a SITREP add to a film for tribal communities?
faq.a: It finds the real barrier before we film. For ITCA's WIC program, our research showed the problem was trust, not awareness, and that changed the whole direction of the films.

work.title: Your Voice, Your Power: Full Episode

industries.about: We make these films with the Inter Tribal Council of Arizona, and community members always tell the story themselves. Here's an episode of Your Voice, Your Power, our docuseries on tribal voting:
industries.heading: Research first, then listen.
industries.approach: Many communities have good reason to doubt messages from outside, so our research looks for that history before we plan anything. That way the film speaks to it instead of around it. Leaders, elders, mothers and young voters speak for themselves, with no outside narrator. We film where people live and work, and we ask before we point a camera at anything. Here's some of the work we've made together:
points: We work with tribal governments, councils and tribal health programs.
We do the research first, then film leaders and community members telling their own stories, on location.
We make public health, education, civic and cultural films.
The films play at community events, in clinics, on tribal media and across social.

industries.name: Government & Public Affairs
industries.text: We make civic, public health and policy films for public agencies and the organizations that work alongside them.
industries.title: Public work, explained plainly.
industries.headline: Public affairs video
industries.intro: Public work only matters if people understand it and show up for it. With the Inter Tribal Council of Arizona, we made Your Voice, Your Power, a 10-part docuseries on tribal voting, and vaccine education for its Tribal Epidemiology Center. We also made Protect Our Land for Paradise Valley Mountain Preserve Trust.

faq.q: Have you made civic engagement films?
faq.a: Yes. Your Voice, Your Power is a 10-part docuseries we made with ITCA Native Vote about tribal voting, told by tribal leaders and voters themselves.

faq.q: How do you handle public health topics like vaccines?
faq.a: Carefully, and research first. For ITCA's Tribal Epidemiology Center, our research showed standard messaging had backfired, so we filmed tribal health leaders and community members explaining vaccines in their own words.

work.title: Your Voice, Your Power: Full Episode

industries.about: Civic films work when people hear from their own neighbors and leaders. Here's an episode of Your Voice, Your Power, the docuseries on tribal voting we made with ITCA Native Vote:
industries.heading: Trust is earned, not announced.
industries.approach: People have heard plenty of official messages, so our SITREP research looks for what they already believe, and why, before we plan anything. Then we let community members, health leaders and local voices explain it in their own words, with no outside narrator talking down to anyone. We check every fact with your team, keep the language plain and make the next step clear: register, get the shot or come to the meeting. Here's some of that work:
points: We work with public agencies, tribal governments and the organizations that work alongside them.
We do the research first, check every fact with your team and let community voices carry the message.
We make civic engagement films, public health education, PSAs and docuseries.
The films play at community events, in clinics, in briefings, on local media and across social.

industries.name: Medical
industries.text: We make patient stories, product launches and procedure explainers with the care and accuracy medicine asks for.
industries.title: Care and accuracy, on camera.
industries.intro: Medicine is hard to film well. The science has to be right, patients have to feel safe, and the film still has to hold someone's attention. We've done it for Boston Scientific, Thermo Fisher and Nektar, for Andres Plastic Surgery, and for clinics and practices across Phoenix.

faq.q: Can you film in a hospital or clinic?
faq.a: Yes. We work around patients and staff, follow your facility's rules and bring only the crew the shot needs. Tell us the restrictions early and we'll plan the shoot around them.

faq.q: Do you make videos for medical device and biotech companies?
faq.a: We do. We've made product films and patient stories for companies like Boston Scientific and Nektar, with shorter cuts for sales teams, conferences and social.

industries.about: Medicine is hard to film well, because the science has to be right and patients have to feel safe. Here's Mike's story, which we made with Nektar:
industries.heading: The science has to be right.
industries.approach: We check every claim with your team before anything ships, and we build the review rounds into the schedule instead of squeezing them in at the end. On set we keep things quiet, explain everything up front and never push for a moment someone isn't ready to share. Then we turn procedures and mechanisms into clear pictures and plain words, so a patient, a buyer or a board member gets it the first time. Here are a few of the films we've made in medicine:
points: We work with hospitals, clinics, specialty and surgical practices, and medical device and biotech companies.
We film patients, clinicians, procedures and products, and we handle all of it with discretion.
We make patient stories, launches, explainers and recruiting films.
The films play in waiting rooms, at conferences, with sales teams and on social.

industries.name: Education & research
industries.text: We explain science, research and learning on camera, from the lab to the classroom, in plain words.
industries.title: Hard ideas, made simple.
industries.headline: Education and research video
industries.intro: Good research and good teaching both deserve a good explanation. We've told a patient's story for Nektar's cancer research, helped the Inter Tribal Council of Arizona's Tribal Epidemiology Center explain vaccines to its own communities and filmed mentoring with New Pathways For Youth.

faq.q: Can you make a video essay or explainer about our research?
faq.a: Yes. We read the papers, talk to the people who did the work and build the story around one clear idea, with graphics where they help.

faq.q: Do you work with schools and universities?
faq.a: Yes. We make recruiting films, program films and explainers, and we plan around class schedules and campus rules.

industries.about: The best explanations come from the people who know the work best. Here's Mike's Story, which we made with Nektar about a melanoma treatment:
industries.heading: Check the facts, then tell the story.
industries.approach: We read before we film, so we can ask the questions a curious viewer would. We check every fact with the people on the record, and we let researchers, teachers and students explain things in their own words. Then we keep only what helps someone understand. Here are a few of the films we've made to teach:
points: We work with universities, schools, labs, research teams, health educators and youth programs.
We read up on the subject, check every fact and let the experts explain it in their own words.
We make explainers, video essays, research stories, training films and recruiting films.
The films play in classrooms and trainings, at conferences, in grant reports and online.

industries.name: Tech
industries.text: We explain products and platforms simply, with real people at the center.
industries.title: Complex, made simple.
industries.intro: Software is hard to film because the product lives on a screen. We put real people at the center instead, with work for companies like Uber, Opendoor, Ridgeline and Medaire.

faq.q: Do you make SaaS explainer videos?
faq.a: Yes. We make explainers, launch films and customer stories built around real people rather than screen recordings alone. For Medaire, we made a product film its sales team uses to pitch and demo.

faq.q: Can you film our team and customers on location?
faq.a: Yes, in Phoenix or wherever they are. We bring the crew and gear to your office, a customer's site or your event, like the family pop-up we filmed for Opendoor in Phoenix.

We put the people who build and use the product ahead of the screens.

industries.name: Professional Services
industries.text: We make films for financial, accounting and law firms, where trust is the product and every frame has to earn it.
industries.title: Trust, on screen.
industries.headline: Professional services video
industries.intro: In professional services, trust is the product. Whether it's a wealth manager, an accounting firm or a law practice, people want to meet the team before the first meeting. We've made films for UBS, State Farm, 1st Bank, Questage and Payroc, including a team film for Finnerty Partners, a UBS Private Wealth Management team that oversees $914 million in client assets.

faq.q: Do you work with wealth management teams?
faq.a: Yes. Our film for Finnerty Partners, a UBS team, lets prospective clients feel the service before the first meeting.

faq.q: How do you handle compliance review?
faq.a: We build review rounds into the schedule and keep every claim in the script, where your compliance team or your firm's counsel can check it before we shoot.

industries.about: In professional services, trust is the product, so we make films that let people meet the team before the first meeting. Here's the one we made for Finnerty Partners at UBS:
industries.heading: Polished, but still human.
industries.approach: We plan scripts and claims with your compliance team from the start, so approvals don't stall the edit. Advisors, accountants and attorneys aren't actors, so we coach on camera and keep interviews conversational until busy people look at ease. The look is clean and premium, but it still feels human, because clients pick people, not logos. Here are a few of the films we've made for professional firms:
points: We work with wealth managers, banks, insurers and advisors, and we bring the same care to accounting and law firms.
We film polished interviews and team films, with compliance and your profession's rules in mind from the start.
We make team and service films, client education, explainers and recruiting films.
The films play in client meetings, in proposals, on your website and in recruiting.

industries.name: Sports
industries.text: We film athletes, teams and events with the same energy they bring to the field.
industries.title: Energy you can feel.
industries.intro: Sport is fast, loud and over in a second. We bring crews that keep up, with slow motion, aerials and specialty rigs, for names like the NFL, UFC and Golf Digest and companies like Training Mask and Fuji Sports.

faq.q: Do you shoot slow motion and aerials?
faq.a: Yes. High-speed cameras, drones and cable cams are part of our kit, and the people running them have used them for a decade.

faq.q: Can you film live games and events?
faq.a: Yes. We plan coverage with the venue, then deliver highlights and social cuts fast, sometimes the same night.

industries.about: Sport is fast and over in a second, so we bring crews and rigs that keep up. Here's Learn To Breathe, which we shot for Training Mask:
industries.heading: Game day only happens once.
industries.approach: We scout, plan coverage and run more than one angle, so the big moment never gets missed. High-speed cameras and careful light turn sweat and impact into something worth replaying. Athletes don't have much time to give, so we run tight, fast sets and get the shots without wearing anyone out. Here's what that looks like:
points: We work with teams, leagues, athletes, gyms and the companies that make sports gear.
We bring fast-moving crews, slow motion and specialty rigs to game day and the gym.
We make promos, athlete features, product films and highlights.
The films play on social, on arena screens, on product pages and with the media covering the game.

industries.name: Live Events
industries.text: We cover festivals, concerts and conferences, from multi-camera coverage to the aftermovie everyone shares.
industries.title: Relive it. Then sell the next one.
industries.intro: Festivals and live events are made to be felt, not explained. We've made aftermovies for Relentless Beats festivals like Decadence Arizona and Gold Rush, filmed Wonderspaces' immersive art shows and traveled to Ireland with Music Celebrations International.

faq.q: How fast can we get an aftermovie?
faq.a: Fast. We plan the edit before the event, so social clips can go out within days, sometimes the same night, with the full recap close behind.

faq.q: Can you cover multi-day festivals?
faq.a: Yes. Decadence Arizona runs two nights across four stages at Phoenix Raceway, and we've made its aftermovies.

quote.text: They are so talented and creative...they take our vision and really make it come to life with the videos they have created for MCI.

A good aftermovie is also the first invitation to next year's event, so we cut it to make everyone who missed it want a ticket. Here are a few of the nights we've filmed:
points: We work with festivals, promoters, conferences and venues.
We bring multi-camera coverage and aerials, and we edit fast, sometimes the same night.
We make aftermovies, recaps, promos and social cuts.

industries.name: Arts & culture
industries.text: We film music, museums, art spaces and performances, and the artists who make them.
industries.title: Made to be felt.
industries.headline: Arts and culture video
industries.intro: Art is hard to describe and easy to feel, so we film it the way it feels in the room. We've filmed the immersive shows at Wonderspaces, followed Music Celebrations International's musicians to Ireland and made aftermovies for Relentless Beats.

faq.q: Do you make music videos?
faq.a: Yes. We plan the concept with the artist, shoot it like a short film and cut it to the music.

faq.q: Can you film inside a museum or gallery?
faq.a: Yes. We work around open hours, light without harming the work and keep crews small so the space stays calm.

industries.about: Art spaces are made to be walked through, so we move the camera the way a visitor would. Here's Immerse Yourself, which we made for Wonderspaces:
industries.heading: Let the work speak.
industries.approach: We spend time with the work before we film it, so the camera knows where to look. We respect the artist's vision and keep our hands off the parts that make it theirs. And we cut to the rhythm of the piece, whether that's a song, a performance or a room full of light. Here are a few of the pieces we've filmed:
points: We work with musicians, artists, museums, galleries, art spaces and performing arts groups.
We plan with the artist, then shoot it like a short film, with light, movement and sound that match the work.
We make music videos, exhibition films, performance films, artist profiles and promos.
The films play on streaming and social, in galleries and lobbies and in grant and sponsor pitches.

industries.name: Food & hospitality
industries.text: We film kitchens, dining rooms, hotels and the people behind them, so people can almost taste it before they book.
industries.title: Make them almost taste it.
industries.intro: Cooking is one of the oldest arts there is, and every kitchen has a story behind it. We film chefs, restaurants and food makers so viewers can almost taste what's on the plate, like our work for High Vibe Kitchen and PB Americano.

faq.q: Can you film while we're open?
faq.a: Usually, yes. We plan around service, keep the crew out of the way and save the big setups for quiet hours.

faq.q: What do restaurants and food makers usually ask for?
faq.a: Usually one main film about the people and the place, a stack of short social cuts and stills from the same shoot, so the menu, the website and the feed all stay fresh.

industries.about: People eat with their eyes first, so we film the food and the feeling, not just the room. Here's Take a Little Trip, which we made for High Vibe Kitchen:
industries.heading: Film the feeling, not the room.

industries.intro: Construction and manufacturing are done by crews, and crews make great stories. We've filmed for Rumco, IMS Builders and Citgo and Brundage Bone, from the job site to the finished build, and we bring the same approach to plants, yards and the people who run them.

faq.q: Can you film on an active job site or plant floor?
faq.a: Yes. We plan with your safety lead, wear the gear, bring only the crew we need and shoot around the work.

faq.q: What do construction and manufacturing companies use video for?
faq.a: Mostly company and culture films, recruiting, project recaps and safety training. Rumco's films cover both its company story and its internal operations.

industries.about: Building and making things is done by crews, and crews make great stories. Here's Building With Integrity, one of the films we made for Rumco:

industries.approach: We follow your site rules, wear the gear and work around live equipment without slowing the job. Aerials and wide moves show the size of the work in a way a phone photo never will. Hiring is hard, too, and a film that shows real crews and real pride does more for recruiting than any job post. cases.title: Dear Mom
cases.text: Tribal mothers speak straight to other mothers, so families trust WIC enough to enroll.
cases.story: The Inter Tribal Council of Arizona's WIC program had eligible families who weren't enrolling. Our SITREP research found the barrier was trust, not awareness. So we put tribal mothers on camera talking straight to other mothers, with no narration and no institutional voice, and we shot them in unbroken takes so they read as neighbors.

stats.label: ITCA WIC participation, FY2024 to FY2025: its first rise after two years of decline
Average women, infants and children on ITCA WIC each month in FY2025
WIC participation nationwide, FY2022 to FY2025

cases.lede: Tribal mothers speak straight to other mothers, so families trust WIC enough to enroll.
sitrep: When ITCA came to us, its WIC program needed more families enrolled. Participation had been falling even though plenty of families were eligible.
Our research found that many tribal members linked WIC with government surveillance. The barrier wasn't awareness, it was trust.
So we filmed tribal mothers speaking straight to camera in unbroken takes, with no narration and no institutional framing.

process.name: Idea
process.text: Bring us an idea, a brief or a blank page, and we'll find the story in it together.
process.more: It starts with a call. Bring us a spark, a brief or a blank page, and we'll talk it through until we know what's worth saying.

process.name: Discovery
process.text: We listen first: to your people, your history and what you hope the film will do.
process.more: We listen first: to your people, your history, the people you want to reach and what you hope to leave behind. You come away with a clear plan, a schedule and a budget.

process.name: SITREP
process.text: We research your craft, your peers and your industry, then bring you a point of view on the story.
process.more: SITREP is our research. Before we film, we dig into your craft, your peers, your industry and the wider sector, like an outside R&D department that cares about your story as much as you do. Then we bring you a point of view and help steer the film toward the story worth telling.

process.name: Production
process.text: Our crew shoots it with cinema cameras and real care, on location or in the studio.
process.more: Our crew shoots with cinema cameras, lighting and sound, on location or in the studio.

process.name: Completion
process.text: We edit, color, mix and deliver it, and we make it to hold up for years.
process.more: We edit, color and mix the film, then cut a version for every place it needs to play. We make it to hold up for years, not just for launch week.
